headings.title: SMTO-CTX-0028 — SMTO couldn't find an item in this Task's saved notes

html:
SMTO-CTX-0028 — SMTO couldn't find an item in this Task's saved notes

GUID: 5fe6334c-9fa2-5ba8-bb55-36cbbdb9933e
Slug: task-context-lookup-unavailable
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: task_context

What happened

  • SMTO tried to open a saved note, result or page from this Task, but it was not available. It may have changed, expired or been removed. This lookup changed nothing, and it doesn't mean earlier work failed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If the Task is still running, wait for it. SMTO is shown which notes it can open, and usually finds the right one on the next step. This is a warning about one lookup, and SMTO gets directions to an available note.
  2. If you saw this after selecting Save to task context or opening Saved task context, reload the page and check that the conversation and its Task still exist. Saved task context only works while its conversation and Task are still there; a deleted or removed Task has none.
  3. Before asking SMTO to repeat a step, scroll up in the conversation and check whether that step already finished, for example a command that ran or a file that changed. A failed lookup doesn't mean the earlier work failed, and repeating it could do the same thing twice.
  4. If the Task was removed, select New chat and describe what you still need. A removed Task's notes can't be reopened, so new work needs a fresh start.

What success looks like

  • SMTO continues the Task using an available note, or the Saved task context panel loads without an error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, saying which conversation you were in. Don't re-run commands or changes from that Task until you've confirmed they didn't already happen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Task Context read, list, search or saved-message request could not resolve the reference, pointer, continuation cursor or notebook under its current scope, revision, retention or access rules.

What this means

  • Task Context could not resolve this bounded lookup under the current notebook scope, revision, retention, or source-field rules. This does not establish that earlier work never happened. It does not authorize replay of external operations.

Why this can happen

  • The source is absent, changed, inaccessible, deleted, or does not provide the requested field.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect error_kind, next_action, available_pointers, and notebook coverage.

How to fix it

  • Follow the tool response's next_action or available_pointers. For invalid_or_stale_cursor, repeat the same read or list without cursor; for intent use current/request or current/original_request; otherwise list an observed section for permitted references. For the saved-messages route (404 task_context_unavailable or task_context_retired), confirm the request still belongs to an existing, non-deleted conversation and a task that was not removed. Never replay external operations because a lookup failed.
  • Use current/request or current/original_request for intent; list an observed section for other permitted references.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a permitted source, available field, or fresh cursor.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected source is returned with explicit coverage and completeness.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat external work because its lookup failed.

Technical notes

  • Do not interpret an unavailable source or empty search as proof of no execution.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
